title: meta-loop wedge: auto-resume in-flight PRD, evented refusals, one state-file owner
description: Three connected defects in the deterministic chain, found in the 2026-07-06 audit when CAM-118 wedged after a cam run restart. (1) Absorbing wedge state: prd.json in flight (stories passes:false) plus phase idle has NO auto-resume path. The sidecar boot does not detect it (src/commands/sidecar.ts:1834-1898 has no re-arm), the meta-loop is gated off by prdInFlight (src/supervisor/loop.ts:1762-1767), and handleBlockedCycleBoundary treats prd-present as cycle-in-flight and skips silently (src/commands/sidecar.ts:1204-1206). Only operator cam next recovers. Observed live: CAM-118 planned plus audited, wedged idle. (2) Unevented terminals and refusals: finishTerminal('blocked') never calls logEvent (src/supervisor/loop.ts:725-728); cycle-in-flight, merge-watch-present and phase-not-idle skips are silent; there is no meta-loop-refused or cycle-wedged event kind and no durable marker for an implement-blocked terminal (contrast .cam-ship-stalled.json). The two failure modes that produced the incident are exactly the two without events. (3) cam-loop.local.md has three uncoordinated owners: phase setters (sidecar.ts:587-654), clearActive which rewrites the file omitting phase so it collapses to idle (sidecar.ts:305-352 plus renderStateFile in src/commands/next.ts:106-110, same mechanism as CAM-191 lost phase:shipping), and the orchestrator pane wrapper which rm -f the file on orch exit (src/commands/run.ts:283), deleting a live cycle signal under the running sidecar (the trigger of this wedge). Minor rider: meta-loop dispatch has no pending-guard; mutex-busy resets phase to idle and the dispatcher re-fires every ~4.7s (approx 20 dispatched:true events for CAM-98 on 2026-07-06); add a pending-guard or throttle. Fix direction: (a) at sidecar boot and idle-tick, detect in-flight PRD with pending stories plus idle phase and re-arm implementing with cam next semantics, gated on the same drain preconditions; (b) emit events for every terminal and refusal path plus a durable blocked marker the orchestrator reads at boot; (c) make the state-file lifecycle single-owner: the wrapper must never delete a live cycle signal. Cross-refs: CAM-191 (clearActive phase-drop), CAM-192 (image-stale block that started the incident).

acceptanceCriteria: renderStateFile (src/commands/next.ts) is read-modify-write: an absent phase preserves the current file's phase; an explicit phase wins; a nonexistent file defaults to idle. clearActive (src/commands/sidecar.ts) no longer collapses phase to idle, and the CAM-191 reorder workaround is retired.

The orchestrator-pane exit wrapper (src/commands/run.ts) never deletes .claude/cam-loop.local.md (the rm -f is removed); the live cycle signal survives an orchestrator recycle under a running sidecar.

The sidecar re-arms implementing at both boot and idle-tick when prd.json is in-flight (>=1 non-operator story with passes:false) AND phase==implementing AND the loop is not already active, gated on the same drain preconditions as meta-loop dispatch (no blocked terminal, no pending merge-watch, no plan/ship phase in progress). phase:idle is the parked discriminator and never auto-resumes.

finishTerminal (src/supervisor/loop.ts) emits a structured logEvent carrying the terminal reason, so every terminal (blocked, complete, awaiting-operator, max-iterations) records a flight-recorder line.

A durable marker .cam-implement-blocked.json is written on the blocked terminal ({ issueId, story, reason, writtenAt }), mirroring .cam-ship-stalled.json; the orchestrator reads it at boot and surfaces an implement-blocked blocker line; it is consumed/cleared by the next implement run for that issue.

Every currently-silent skip/refusal path (the plain in-flight skip in handleBlockedCycleBoundary, cycle-in-flight, merge-watch-present, phase-not-idle) emits a meta-loop-dispatch event with a structured reason enum; no new event kinds are invented.

A per-issue pending-guard in DispatchClosureState suppresses re-dispatch of the same issue until its cycle reaches a terminal (mirroring the existing stopped/drained/blockedCycle dedup); the idle-tick checks re-arm before meta-loop dispatch.
spec.scope: Close the meta-loop wedge (CAM-118 incident) as one coherent PRD covering all three connected defects plus the dispatch-throttle rider. The three defects are coupled through the cam-loop.local.md phase field and the sidecar idle/active loop, so a partial fix leaves the wedge reachable. Defect 3 (state-file single-owner: phase preservation + no wrapper delete) is the root and a precondition for Defect 1 (boot/idle-tick re-arm keyed on phase==implementing, with phase:idle as the parked discriminator). Defect 2 (event on every terminal + durable implement-blocked marker + evented refusal paths) is the observability that would have surfaced the incident, and it overlaps Defect 1's handleBlockedCycleBoundary path. The rider adds a per-issue pending-guard to stop the dispatched-path re-fire. Touches ~5-7 source files: sidecar.ts, loop.ts, events.ts, next.ts, run.ts, a new implement-blocked marker module, and the orchestrator boot-read surface.
gotchas: The new .cam-implement-blocked.json marker must be surfaced by the orchestrator boot-read, whose documentation lives in templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md (and its embedded copy). Any edit under templates/ requires bun run embed-vendor + embed-vendor:check or the byte-parity gate fails and plan preflight aborts.

The re-arm (in-flight PRD resume) and the meta-loop dispatch (new backlog issue) both write the phase field; on the idle-tick, re-arm must be checked before dispatch so a resumable in-flight PRD is not shadowed by a new dispatch.

phase:idle as the parked/no-resume discriminator is only trustworthy because of the phase-preservation fix (renderStateFile read-modify-write) and the wrapper no longer deleting the file; the three defects must ship together.

CAM-191 (shipped) only reordered phase:shipping to survive teardown; it deliberately left the renderStateFile/clearActive phase-drop in place. Retiring that workaround is in scope and must not regress the ship-phase survival CAM-191 secured.
